answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents post stake to audit transactions across a topological cut verification protocol. When auditors verify graph connectivity, any partition attempt triggers game-theoretic multi-agent cross-auditing. If fraudulent identities coordinate on a malicious network knoll or try bridging the partition ridge, honest verifiers detect the inconsistency and execute stake slashing, turning attacker deposits into burned umber records. This topological verification forces attacker costs to scale superlinear with network size.
